tasks.short: Monitor the ethical environment in person

steps.what: List open concerns from the ethics log
Monitor the ethical environment in person
Ensure a sound response is recorded

tasks.design: Open concerns are listed from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Monitoring the ethical environment stays in person. The security manager records the response. The list does not judge a person, and it is not a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Concerns were side conversations with no list of what was still open.
tasks.enabler_now: An open concern can be listed without naming a finding.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the environment is sound stays something the manager watches.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears what a log line cannot hold.
tasks.altitude: Open concerns are visible. The watching, and any response, stay with the manager.

reach.learn: What was not treated as a concern

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. A concern list is not a judgement of a person.

The source pack names a rule that a significant decision about a person is not taken by automation alone, and that hiring, appraisal, or staff monitoring needs works-council consent. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when an ethics concern is logged and ends when the manager records the response.
A concern has an id, a date, and a short type, produced by the person who logged it. It does not contain a score. A concern about a named person is not decided by the list.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Who may log a concern, and who may read it.
research_questions: Does staff monitoring of this kind already have works-council consent?

already_counted.description: Watching the environment is already in the monitoring step.

incremental.description: Withdraw a response record if the concern is closed as mistaken.

approvals.approved_version: response the manager recorded for that concern

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when concerns are only spoken. No score is written. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review security documents before they are issued

steps.what: Gather incident facts for the document
Draft incident reports from stored facts

loop.purpose: Draft security documents that cite only stored incident facts.
loop.input: Incident id and the fact text the manager marked usable.
loop.output: Draft paragraphs that each cite an incident id.
loop.check: Every paragraph cites a marked fact, and no initiative is invented.
loop.stop: Stop when no fact is marked usable.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template report cannot show which incident a sentence came from.

tasks.design: Incident facts the manager has marked are gathered from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A draft report cites only those facts. The security manager reviews tactical or strategic initiatives, and only that review is issued as the security documents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incident reports were rewritten from memory for each proposal.
tasks.enabler_now: A fact can be marked usable and cited by id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether an initiative is sound stays a review.
tasks.human_edge: The manager rejects a sentence the facts do not support.

ambition.what: A new marked fact can refresh the draft the same week, and an unmarked fact is not written in.

tasks.altitude: The week is the review of initiatives, not the retyping of known facts.

evidence.claim: A document that cites marked incident ids can be checked sentence by sentence. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when a security document is requested and ends when the manager issues it.
A fact has an incident id and a usable flag set by the manager. The draft ignores unmarked facts and does not propose an initiative.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Who is allowed to mark a fact as usable.
research_questions: Which documents must leave the security team, and which stay internal?

already_counted.description: Reviewing initiatives is already in the review step.

incremental.description: Retire a document when a cited fact is corrected.

approvals.approved_version: documents the manager reviewed for those facts

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when facts are not marked. The review stays. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate security status under a protocol

steps.what: Assemble status figures from the incident log
Draft status updates from stored figures

loop.purpose: Draft a status update that cites only stored figures and the protocol id.
loop.input: Figure id, value, and protocol id.
loop.output: Update lines that cite a figure id and the protocol.
loop.check: Every number cites a stored figure, and no problem is added.
loop.stop: Stop when the protocol id is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A free message cannot show which figure a number came from.

steps.what: Decide which potential problems to communicate
Send the security update by protocol

tasks.design: Status figures are assembled from the {OPS_SYSTEM} log onto {BI}. A draft update cites only those figures and the protocol. The security manager decides which potential problems to communicate, and that version is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status notes were typed from memory against a protocol in a drawer.
tasks.enabler_now: Figures and a protocol id can be stored and cited.
tasks.still_hard: Which problem is real enough to communicate stays a decision.
tasks.human_edge: The manager withholds a figure the protocol does not allow.

ambition.what: A figure change can refresh the draft the same day, and an undecided problem is not sent.

tasks.altitude: The week is choosing what to say, not retyping the counts.

evidence.claim: A status line that cites a stored figure can be checked. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when a status update is due and ends when the manager sends it.
A figure has an id and a value, produced by the incident log. A protocol has an id and a list of allowed figure ids. A figure outside that list is not drafted.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether a written protocol already names the allowed figures.
research_questions: Who receives a status update, inside or outside the firm?

already_counted.description: Choosing problems is already in the decision step.

incremental.description: Retract an update if a cited figure is corrected.

approvals.approved_version: update the manager chose for that protocol

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when figures are not in the log. An undecided problem is not sent. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train people in security rules in person

steps.what: List members due for rules and procedures
Train subordinate security professionals in person

tasks.design: Members due for security rules and procedures are listed from the {LMS}. Training subordinate security professionals stays in person. Attendance of organization members is recorded without a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due lists were a spreadsheet, and attendance was a sign-in sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: A due row can name the person and the rule module.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the rules stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees who did not understand, which attendance cannot show.
tasks.altitude: The due list is current. Training stays in person, and attendance is not a score.

reach.learn: Attendance is not a performance judgement

evidence.claim: A due list and an attendance row are configuration. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. They are not an appraisal.

The source pack names a rule that a significant decision about a person is not taken by automation alone, and that hiring, appraisal, or staff monitoring needs works-council consent. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a rules session is due and ends when attendance is recorded.
A due row has a person id and a module id, produced by the learning record. Attendance stores present or absent. It stores no score and no ranking.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether rule modules already exist as named records.
research_questions: Does recording attendance need works-council consent here?

already_counted.description: Teaching time is already in the training step.

incremental.description: Correct an attendance row marked on the wrong session.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when modules are not named. Training stays in person. No score is stored. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The ethical environment is watched in person, and a concern list is not a score. Documents cite marked facts. Status updates follow the protocol. Training is delivered in person and attendance is not a score.
reach: The director sees the issued document, not the draft.
People management sees attendance, not a ranking.
skills_to_grow: Leave a fact unmarked rather than writing it in.
Do not store a score against a training row.
role.ambitious_version: A newly marked fact refreshes a draft the same week, and an undecided problem is not sent.
